text:
Priya: Hey team, our app started failing calls to the embeddings endpoint about an hour ago. Clients are getting a 400/422 with a message like `dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 1024`. Also seeing big latency spikes (p90 ~2.3s) on the /v1/embeddings route. We use the hosted API with model `embed-small-1024` in one service and `embed-large-1536` in another — could this be a routing issue? Example curl we sent:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large-1536","input":["hello world"]}'
```

Priya: attaching the exact error payload we got from the client lib: `{"error":"dimension_mismatch","expected":1536,"received":1024,"request_id":"rwd_87a2f"}`. We also batch on our side (batch_size=64) to save cost. Rolling back batching reduces failures but throughput suffers.

Aisha: thanks Priya, sorry about the disruption. quick triage questions: 1) are the failing requests all from the same service / deploy? 2) can you paste the `request_id` and the model string used when you see the error? 3) do you have a request trace id or `X-Request-Id` header to tie to logs?

Priya: failures came from the ingestion worker (deploy tag `ingest-1.7.3`). Sample request_id `rwd_87a2f`. Model in the error was `redwood-embed-large-1536`. I also see intermittently "504 gateway timeout" in our logs when we enabled batching; single item calls are usually fine.

Aisha: OK escalting to eng-ml — @Jin can you take a look? My suspicion: dimension mismatch implies a model mismatch between client-side assumption and what our router served (or a payload that included mixed-dimension vectors during an upsert/compare). Also batching can change how we route (different pool).

IncidentBot: Ticket #INC-10431 created for thread 1757604321 — assigned to eng-ml.

Jin: jumping in. thanks for the details. a few debugging steps I want from you, Priya: 1) can you reproduce with a single curl and send the full headers including `User-Agent` and any `X-Trace-Id`? 2) capture the response headers (we set `X-Rw-Model` and `X-Rw-Node` on the response currently) so we can confirm which backend served it. 3) if possible, run with `trace=true` query param or `X-Trace-Id` header and paste the trace id.

Jin: quick notes for the team: dimension mismatch almost always means the upstream model that answered the request has a different embedding dimension than the client expects. Possible causes: - stale client config using an old model name - router fallback to a cheaper/smaller model under capacity pressure - a bug in batch assembly that mixes different model requests into one batch (shouldn't happen but worth verifying). Also batching can add queue time and increase p90 due to head-of-line blocking.

Priya: here's a repro curl that errors for me every time (single item):

```bash
curl -i -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings?trace=true' \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxxx' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'User-Agent: ingest-service/1.7.3' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large-1536","input":["test text"]}'
```

Response headers I captured: `X-Rw-Model: redwood-embed-small-1024`, `X-Rw-Node: rnode-12`, body -> `{"error":"dimension_mismatch","expected":1536,"received":1024,"request_id":"rwd_87a2f"}`. So looks like the router sent it to `redwood-embed-small-1024` even though I asked for `redwood-embed-large-1536`.

Jin: that header is gold — confirms router mismatch. Two follow-ups: 1) check routing policy for your account (some customers have cost-based routing enabled which allows fallback to smaller variants). 2) I'll check if there was a recent rollout that changed model alias mapping; also check if model aliases (e.g., `embed-large`) map to multiple variants.

Samir: adding SRE perspective — the p90 jump may be related to batch queueing. please collect the per-request latency breakdown from our observability: we have the following spans/panels to look at: `embeddings.request.total.latency`, `embeddings.queue.wait_time`, `embeddings.batch.assemble_time`, `embeddings.network.send_recv`, `embeddings.model.inference_time`. Can Priya attach a few `X-Rw-Trace` ids and I'll pull spans.

Samir: recommended quick dashboards/queries (Console -> Observability -> Embedings):
- Panel: Embeddings per-request latency (p50/p90/p99) filter by `route:/v1/embeddings` and `env:prod`
- Panel: Embeddings queue time histogram -> metric `embeddings.queue.wait_time`
- Panel: Batch size distribution -> metric `embeddings.batch.size` (histogram)
- Panel: Backend model mapping -> logs query `X-Rw-Model` grouped by `status_code`

Jin: followup actions we should do asap: 1) verify alias mapping config (did a recent change map `redwood-embed-large-1536` to a family including `redwood-embed-small-1024`?) 2) add a temporary hard deny for fallback for Priya's org id so she gets explicit 4xx instead of silently routing to a different-dim model. 3) add an ingest-time check in the router that verifies model signature/dim and returns 409 if mismatch (we currently rely on model names).

Aisha: Priya — for immediate mitigation you can: 1) explicitly pin to the exact model variant by using the full name (looks like you already do), 2) set account-level policy to disallow cost-fallbacks in the Console (if enabled for your org), or 3) reduce batch size to 1 temporarily while we fix routing to avoid mixed routing/batching interactions.

Jin: Samir — can you pull traces for `rwd_87a2f` and `rwd_87a30` (Priya provided two ids in DM) and check whether batch assembly mixed different model requests? I'm particularly worried about the batcher keying function.

Samir: pulling now — getting spans. initial observation: for request `rwd_87a2f` the trace shows `queue.wait_time` 320ms, `batch.assemble_time` 18ms, `model.inference_time` 1.1s. The `X-Rw-Model` in the selected backend is `redwood-embed-small-1024`. There's a router decision span that shows fallback policy `cost_fallback:true` and `fallback_target:redwood-embed-small-1024`. So it was intentional fallback. That explains the dimension mismatch.

Samir: we should still prevent silent fallbacks for embeddings because mismatch causes clients to break. I'll create a follow-up to change the fallback to an explicit 409 with a helpful message when embedding dimensions differ. For now I can flip the routing policy for org `org_9z` to `no_fallback` (temporary).

Priya: flipping fallback off fixed it on our side — I tested with batch_size=64 and no more dim-mismatch errors, p90 latency improved a bit. Thanks. Any ETA on changing default behavior?

Jin: I'll file a small runtime patch to add embed-dimension validation in the router and return a 409 with `error: embedding_dimension_mismatch` and detail about expected vs requested. Plan: patch + canary -> roll next week. I'll link PR when created.

Samir: I'll add a dashboard tile and an alert: create alert if `error:dimension_mismatch` on embeddings > 1% over 5m for any org. Also add log-based metric for `X-Rw-Model` mismatches so we can surface unintended fallbacks.

Aisha: thanks all. Priya — can you confirm the `org_9z` change fixed your production flow? If yes we'll keep the org override and roll the router change next week.

Priya: confirmed, working now. Please keep me posted on the PR/rollout and if you want a postmortem ping me. Really appreciated the fast turnaround :heart: :thumbsup: 

Aisha: closing the support escalation once the PR is merged and the dashboard + alert are in place. Will follow up in this thread with links.

Jin: PR: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/router/pulls/482 (draft) — adds embed-dimension check and explicit 409 with schema.

Samir: dashboard link (internal): https://console.redwood/dashboards/embeddings?panel=per-request-latency (added tile `Embed: per-request latency breakdown`)

Aisha: note to self: update support runbook with steps to check `X-Rw-Model` header and org-level fallback policy; add snippet to reply template.

Priya: thanks team!
